free_text: The patient is a 66-year-old male with a high PSA of 8.3 and a cT3b prostate cancer, confirmed by a PI-RADS 5 MRI showing extracapsular extension and seminal vesicle involvement. Pathologically, the Gleason score has progressed to 3+5 (ISUP Grade Group 4). Management assessment is pending clinical review regarding individual treatment benefit and patient preferences, balancing aggressive local control against potential side effects.
